Next month at the earliest, Apple is expected to unveil a redesigned next-generation MacBook Pro. At that time, we will see OLED, a touchscreen appearing for the first time on a Mac, a thinner body, Dynamic Island, and more new features. There were earlier rumours that this upgrade would be named MacBook Ultra, but it was not clear at the time what impact it would have on the MacBook Pro brand positioning. Now, things have become much clearer.

At first, everyone might have assumed that the basic 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 chip would continue to carry the MacBook Pro name. Then, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported that Apple would also bring some MacBook Ultra design elements to the basic MacBook Pro equipped with the M7. To me, this news made the 'MacBook Ultra' naming even less likely.

Now, a new report makes the idea of the MacBook Pro and MacBook Ultra co-existing much more plausible.

According to Omdia, Apple will continue to produce its existing miniLED display panels through 2028.

This news means two things: first, if the existing MacBook Pro remains in the product line, the redesigned model is likely to carry a significant premium. Second, the likelihood that the new model will be named MacBook Ultra has also increased substantially.

So, over roughly the next year, the MacBook product line will most likely look something like this:

Autumn 2026:

  • MacBook Neo (A18 Pro)
  • MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, M5)
  • MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch, M6)
  • MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)
  • MacBook Ultra (OLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)

Spring 2027:

  • MacBook Neo (A19 Pro)
  • MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, M6)
  • MacBook Pro (OLED, 14-inch, M7)

Summary

If this all comes true, the MacBook product line will be the most diverse ever. Eventually, the older MacBook Pro should not remain in the line for too long. I think this is part of Apple's strategy to maintain a lower starting price, similar to what they have done in the past.

Under this scenario, I think the starting price for the miniLED version of the MacBook Pro may remain around US$2,499, while the Ultra's starting price would be higher, possibly US$2,999.

What are your thoughts on this rumoured MacBook product line? What do you predict the MacBook Ultra's starting price will be? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
